Base-Mediated Intramolecular Cyclization of α‑Nitroethylallenic
Esters as a Synthetic Route to 5 ‑Hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-ones
Narendra Kumar Vaishanv, Mohd Khalid Zaheer, Sandeep Kumar, Ruchir Kant, and Kishor Mohanan *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2021, 86, 5630 −5638 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: An unprecedented Cs 2CO3-mediated intramolecular cyclization/rearrangement cascade that transforms α-
nitroethylallenic esters to functionalized pyrrolin-2-ones has been uncovered. This reaction provides a new and practical approach
for the synthesis of medicinally privileged 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-ones under mild conditions. The broad potential of this new
method was demonstrated by an e ﬃcient Au/Ag-catalyzed heteroarylation of 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-ones employing electron-rich
heteroarenes to furnish heteroaryl-lactam derivatives.
T
he 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-one is an important class of
heterocyclic compounds frequently encountered in bio-
logically active natural products. 1 Epolactaene, oteromycin,
and pyrrocidine A are some of the selected examples for the
bioactive natural products containing the hydroxypyrrolinone
motif which display neuritogenic as well as other pharmaco-
logical properties ( Figure 1 ).
2 Furthermore, 5-hydroxy-3-
pyrrolin-2-ones have also been employed as a critical
intermediate in the synthesis of various natural products.
3
Consequently, over the past decades, several methods have
been developed to access this important class of compounds.
For instance, intramolecular cyclization reactions, intermolec-
ular reactions, and oxidation of heteroaryls have enabled facile
access to functionalized 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-ones.
4 Among
these methods, intramolecular reactions involving a tethered
amide moiety is the most commonly used approach, and some
selected examples include (i) Cu-catalyzed haloacetamization
of allenamides, (ii) halolactamization of homoallylic amides,
and (iii) the intramolecular radical/enaminic cyclization
reactions of prefunctionalized substrates such as enamides
(Scheme 1 a,b).
5,6 Intermolecular reactions have also provided
straightforward methods to access 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-
ones. The reaction between nitroole ﬁns and 1,3-diketones
7
and the nucleophilic addition/cyclization of amines to MBH
adducts constitute mild routes to hydroxypyrrolinones
(Scheme 1 c).
8 However, the development of novel protocols
to access this class of compounds is always in high demand.
Activated allenes have emerged as a valuable synthon in
organic transformations. 9 In particular, nucleophilic phos-
phine-catalyzed annulation reactions involving allenic esters
have been extensively explored for the construction of a variety
of carbo- and heterocycles.
10 Besides nucleophilic phosphine
catalysis, the synthesis of heterocycles through the base-
mediated reaction of various nucleophiles or electrophiles to
allenic esters have also been explored, though to a limited
extent.
11 In 2006, the Shi group disclosed a carbonate-
catalyzed cyclization reaction of salicylic aldehydes with allenic
ester to obtain chromene derivatives in good to excellent
yield.12 Subsequently, Selig, Zhou, and Rouh demonstrated the
utility of base-mediated re actions of allenic esters in
constructing various heterocyclic compounds such as quino-
lines, benzooxazepino[5,4- a]isoindolone, and functionalized
chromene and chroman derivatives. 13−15 The Kwon group
recently disclosed an interesting phosphine-catalyzed intra-
molecular cyclization of α-nitroethylallenic esters to access
ﬁve-membered cyclic N-hydroxyimidic acid esters. 16 However,
it remained as the only report on the reactivity of α-
nitroethylallenic esters, and related cyclization reactions
under basic conditions are unknown. Our investigations in
this direction culminated in a straightforward single-step
synthesis of 5-hydroxy-3 - p y r r o l i n - 2 - o n e sv i aaC s2CO3-
mediated intramolecular cyclization of α-nitroethylallenic
esters ( Scheme 1 d).

With these precedents in hand, we commenced our study by
examining the reaction of ethyl 2-(2-nitro-1-phenylethyl) buta-
2,3-dienoate 1a with CsF in CH 3CN at room temperature. To
our surprise, the substrate underwent an unexpected intra-
molecular cascade reaction to form 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-one
2a in 66% yield ( Table 1 , entry 1). This unprecedented result
prompted us to screen the reaction parameters in greater detail
to improve the reaction e ﬃciency. Preliminary solvent
screening indicated that CH
3CN was optimal among a variety
of solvents (entries 1 −8). Subsequently, the in ﬂuence of
various organic and inorganic bases in CH 3CN was
investigated. The use of inorganic bases such as t-BuOK,
KOH, NaOH, and K 2CO3 provided the product in moderate
yields, while Cs 2CO3 gave a better yield, in short reaction time
(entries 9 −13). There was no improvement in the e ﬃciency
when the reaction was tried using organic bases such as DMAP
and DABCO (entries 14,15). The product 2a was obtained
only in low yield when we attempted to render the reaction
substoichiometric by employing 0.5 equiv of Cs
2CO3 (entry
16). Moreover, no product yield enhancement was observed
when the reaction was carried out at a higher temperature.
Having the optimal conditions identi ﬁed, we set out to
assess the generality of the present method with respect to
various substitution patterns on the α-nitroethylallenic esters
for the construction of hydroxypyrrolinones, and the results are
summarized in Scheme 2 . Under the standard conditions, a
variety of nitroethylallenic esters, irrespective of the electronic
and steric nature of the substituents they possess, were
converted to the corresponding products in good yields.
Aromatic rings bearing electronically varied substituents such
as methoxy, thiomethyl, bromo, chloro, and ﬂuoro at the para-
position of the phenyl ring were very well tolerated and
provided the desired products in good to excellent yields ( 2b−
h). The structure of the product 2f was unambiguously
conﬁrmed by X-ray analysis. Delightfully, the transformation
was e ﬀective for substrates bearing methoxy as well as halo
substituents at the meta-position ( 2i−k). Furthermore, the
substrates having di- and trisubstituted aromatic rings were
also competent in this reaction, providing the corresponding
products without any deterioration in yield ( 2l−m). The
protocol was also amenable for naphthyl-derived substrates
and furnished the product 2n in 88% yield. Given the ubiquity
of heteroaryls in drug discovery, we evaluated substrates
bearing thiophene and furan for this reaction, and the
corresponding hydroxypyrrolinones were achieved in good
yields ( 2o−q). Finally, we sought to evaluate the substrate

scope by varying the ester moiety of allene 1, and the methyl,
benzyl, and t-butyl esters of allenoate readily underwent the
reaction to furnish the products in good yields ( 2r−t). Our
further attempts to expand the scope of allenoates by
introducing substitution at the γ-position failed to deliver the
anticipated product. On a larger scale, the reaction of
nitroethylallenoate 1a provided the corresponding product
2a in 66% yield.
Next, we focused our attention on further functionalization
of 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-one 2. We anticipated that a π acid
such as PPh
3AuCl might coordinate with the hydroxyl group of
pyrrolinone moiety 2a and generate the N-acyliminium ion,
making it an e ﬀective electrophile for electron-rich heteroaryls.
Given the importance of indoles as a common motif in natural
products and bioactive compounds,
17 we selected 1-methyl-
indole as a model substrate for this reaction. If successful, this
reaction would provide a practical route to indolylpyrrolinones.
Based on these considerations, the reaction of 2a with 1-
methylindole was attempted with catalytic amounts of
PPh
3AuCl and AgOTf in DCM. To our delight, the reaction
proceeded in the expected manner, and indolylpyrrolinone 4a
was obtained in 86% yield ( Scheme 3 ). Notably, N-
unsubstituted indole reacted analogously to a ﬀord product
4b in 77% yield. Moreover, halo substituents at the C5- or C6-
position of the indole ring were tolerated, a ﬀording the
corresponding products in good yields ( 4c, 4d). A bulkier
tetrahydrocyclopentaindole substrate also underwent this
reaction and provided 4e in high yield. The structure of 4e
was conﬁrmed by X-ray crystallographic analysis. The reaction
carried out using 3-methylindole furnished the C2 product 4f
in good yield, illustrating the applicability of this method for
structurally challenging substrates. Other heteroaryl substrates
such as 2-methoxythiophene and 1-methylpyrrole also reacted
smoothly with hydroxypyrrolinone and delivered the products
in good yields ( 4g, 4h).
Besides this, in order to leverage the synthetic utility of the
products in accessing bis-indole alkaloid-like compounds,
18 the
lactam 4b, after the N-Boc protection of both indole and
pyrrole moieties, was subjected to reduction using excess
DIBAL-H. The reduction delivered the hemi aminal 6 as an
inseparable mixture of diastereomers in 5:1 ratio. The product
6 was then treated with N-methylindole, and pleasingly, the
reaction furnished the bisindole derivative 7 in 67% yield,
albeit with low diastereoselectivity ( Scheme 4 ). To further
demonstrate the synthetic relevance of the method, reductive
removal of the hydroxyl group of 2a was performed using
NaCNBH
3, and the corresponding lactam 8 was obtained in
56% yield. Treating 2a with HCl and methanol delivered the
methyl ether 9 in 70% yield.
A plausible mechanism for the formation of 5-hydroxy-3-
pyrrolin-2-ones is outlined in Scheme 5 . First, carbonate-
mediated deprotonation of α-nitroethylallenic ester 1 forms
the corresponding α-nitro anion A. The alternative resonance
form of anion A, nitronate B, engages in intramolecular 1,4-

subsequently isomerizes to give the cyclic nitronate D. The
nitronate D involves a spontaneous ring contraction/
tautomerization process to form the oxime intermediate F.16
Oxime F, under the basic conditions, undergoes ring opening
to give rise to the nitrile intermediate G. Subsequent hydrolysis
of G aﬀords the intermediate H, which tautomerizes to amide
I. Finally, the intramolecular cyclization of I aﬀords the desired
5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-ones 2.
To shed light into the proposed reaction mechanism, the
oxime intermediate F was synthesized using a reported
procedure.16 Pleasingly, the substrate F, when exposed to
Cs2CO3 under the established reaction conditions, readily
transformed into compound 2a in 87% yield. This ascertains
the intermediacy of F in this novel protocol ( Scheme 6 ).

intramolecular transformation of α-nitroethylallenic esters to

wide range of medicinally valuable 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-ones
in good to excellent yield and features a wide substrate scope
and high functional group tolerance. The utility of this method
was subsequently demonstrated by developing an Au/Ag-
catalyzed heteroarylation of 5-hydroxy-3-pyrrolin-2-one to
access densely functionalized heteroaryl-lactam derivatives.
The strategy was subsequently extended to access synthetically
attractive bis-indole-pyrroline derivatives.
■ EXPERIMENTAL SECTION
General Experimental Information. Unless otherwise speci ﬁed,
all reactions were performed under air atmosphere in oven-dried
round-bottom ﬂasks. The reactions were monitored by TLC
visualized by UV (254 nm) and/or with iodine. Column
chromatography was performed on 100 −200 mesh silica gel using
the gradient system ethyl acetate-hexane. The NMR data were
recorded at Bruker AV 400 MHz in CDCl
3/DMSO-d6 using as
internal standards the residual CHCl 3 signal for 1H NMR ( δ = 7.26
ppm) and the deuterated solvent signal for 13C NMR ( δ = 77.16
ppm) and residual DMSO signal for 1H NMR (δ = 2.50 ppm) and the
deuterated solvent signal for 13C NMR ( δ = 39.5 ppm). Coupling
constants are given in Hertz (Hz), and the classical abbreviations are
used to describe the signal multiplicities. Melting points were
measured with a Bu ̈chi B-540 apparatus and are uncorrected. High-
resolution mass spectra were obtained using a Q-TOF mass
spectrometer. All commercially available reagents were used as
received. α-Nitroethylallenic esters 1a−t were synthesized and
characterized by following the procedure reported by the Kwon
group.
16
General Procedure for the Synthesis of 5-Hydroxy-3-
pyrrolin-2-ones 2a −t. To an oven-dried round-bottom ﬂask was
added α-nitroethylallenic ester 1 (0.20 mmol) in CH 3CN and
Cs2CO3 (0.20 mmol). The reaction mixture was stirred at 25 °C for 2
h. After the completion of the reaction, as indicated by TLC, the
reaction mixture was extracted using ethyl acetate (3 × 10 mL) and
water, and the organic layer was washed with saturated brine. Finally,
the organic layer was dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate and
evaporated under reduced pressure. The residue was puri ﬁed using
column chromatography (100 −200 mesh silica gel) using acetone/
dichloromethane as the eluent to a ﬀord the product 2.

20 mL) and water and was washed with saturated brine. Finally, the
organic layer was dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate and evaporated
under reduced pressure. The residue was puri ﬁed using column
chromatography (100 −200 mesh silica gel) using acetone/dichloro-
methane as the eluent to a ﬀord the product 2a in 66% yield (660 mg).
